title: B1 · L8 — Passive: present & past simple
topic: Voz pasiva en presente y pasado simples
description: Formación y uso de la voz pasiva en presente ('is/are + participio') y pasado ('was/were + participio') para enfatizar la acción o el receptor.

questions.prompt: Explicas un dato geográfico sobre idiomas del mundo.
questions.question: Complete: 'English ___ in many countries around the world.'
questions.explanation: Voz pasiva presente simple: 'is/are + participio pasado'. Se usa cuando interesa el receptor de la acción (English), no quién la realiza. Error típico: usar activa 'English speaks' — el idioma no habla, ES hablado. En español pasamos por 'se habla', que corresponde a la pasiva inglesa.
examples: Coffee is grown mainly in Brazil and Colombia. → hecho general
These products are made in Germany, hence the quality. → pasiva descriptiva

questions.prompt: Transformas una frase activa a pasiva para un texto turístico.
questions.question: Choose the passive form of 'They built this bridge in 1990':
options: This bridge has been built in 1990.
questions.explanation: Pasiva pasado simple: 'was/were + participio'. El objeto activo (this bridge) pasa a sujeto pasivo. Error común: (A) olvidar el auxiliar 'was'; (C) usar presente cuando el año fija el pasado; (D) present perfect no encaja con año específico (marcador cerrado).
examples: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci. → hecho histórico
These letters were written in 1850 by an anonymous poet. → obra pasada

questions.statement: The passive voice is used when we want to focus on the action or the object, not on who does the action.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. La pasiva se usa cuando (1) el agente es desconocido, (2) es obvio, (3) es poco importante, o (4) queremos destacar el receptor. En inglés se usa MUCHÍSIMO más que en español — en noticias, ciencia, negocios, procesos.
examples: My car was stolen last night — no idea who. → agente desconocido
The president was elected in a landslide. → foco en el evento

questions.text: The report was written by the marketing team last week.
questions.explanation: Nota el linking 'was-written' con la /s/ y la /r/ fusionadas. 'By the' se pronuncia rápido, casi 'bythe' con schwa. Fórmula clásica en emails y contextos profesionales: 'The [X] was + participio + by [agente] + [tiempo]'.
examples: The email was sent by the manager first thing this morning. → pasiva profesional
The book was translated by a well-known author. → pasiva editorial

questions.prompt: Describes la procedencia de unos coches en una feria.
questions.question: Complete: 'These cars ___ in Japan.'
questions.explanation: 'Are made' → pasiva presente simple para hechos generales. Como 'cars' es plural, va 'are + participio'. Error típico: usar activa ('make', 'makes') tratando al sujeto como agente cuando en realidad es receptor de la acción.
examples: These shoes are made in Italy by hand. → producción actual
This wine is produced in Chile, in the Maipo Valley. → origen habitual

questions.prompt: Empareja cada frase activa con su versión pasiva:

pairs.left: Active: They deliver mail every day.
pairs.right: Passive: Mail is delivered every day.

pairs.left: Active: They built the school in 1980.
pairs.right: Passive: The school was built in 1980.

questions.explanation: La transformación pasiva sigue tres pasos: (1) el objeto activo pasa a sujeto pasivo, (2) el verbo se convierte en 'be + participio' (concordando en tiempo), (3) el agente desaparece o se introduce con 'by + agente'.
examples: They cleaned the house. → The house was cleaned. → objeto se hace sujeto
The teacher explains grammar. → Grammar is explained by the teacher. → foco en el contenido

questions.prompt: Entras al café y encuentras una bolsa en tu silla.
questions.question: Choose the correct passive: 'Someone left this bag here.'
questions.explanation: El agente ('someone') es desconocido → pasiva ideal. Pasado simple pasivo: 'was left'. Errores: (A) sin auxiliar; (C) presente no encaja con evento puntual pasado; (D) 'has left' es agramatical aquí (leave sería intransitivo — la bolsa no se va sola).
examples: The window was broken last night — no idea how. → agente desconocido
My wallet was found in the park, thankfully. → foco en el resultado

questions.target: This café was opened about five years ago and honestly, it's still really popular.
questions.explanation: Situación: le recomiendas un sitio a un amigo turista. Combina pasiva pasado ('was opened') con presente ('is still popular'). Discourse markers 'about' (suaviza cifra) y 'honestly' (aporta credibilidad) hacen el habla natural. Muy útil para hablar de lugares y su historia.
examples: The bridge was built in the 19th century and it's now a huge landmark. → historia + presente
This restaurant was founded by a Spanish chef and it's absolutely loved by locals. → origen + popularidad

questions.statement: In passive sentences, we must always mention the person who does the action using 'by'.
questions.explanation: FALSO. 'By + agente' es OPCIONAL. Se omite cuando el agente es (1) desconocido, (2) obvio, (3) irrelevante. De hecho, en la mayoría de pasivas naturales el 'by' no aparece. Solo se añade si el agente aporta información valiosa.
examples: The letter was sent yesterday. → agente irrelevante (no 'by')
The book was written by Orwell. → agente valioso (sí 'by')

questions.prompt: Cuentas un dato impactante sobre las comunicaciones globales.
questions.question: Complete: 'Millions of emails ___ every second worldwide.'
questions.explanation: 'Are sent' → pasiva presente simple para hechos generales que ocurren habitualmente. 'Emails' plural → 'are'. Error típico: usar activa 'send/sends' tratando a los emails como agentes cuando son receptores de la acción.
examples: Millions of tickets are sold every year at that arena. → dato habitual
Thousands of books are published every month in Spanish. → estadística general

questions.text: The new hospital was opened by the mayor last month.
questions.explanation: Nota el linking 'was-opened' fluido. 'By the mayor' se enlaza con la /ð/ suave. Estructura clásica de noticias sobre inauguraciones oficiales: 'The [instalación] was + participio + by [autoridad] + [momento]'. Muy útil para entender titulares.
examples: The bridge was inaugurated by the president in a formal ceremony. → noticia formal
The exhibition was launched by a famous local artist. → evento cultural

questions.prompt: Identifica la frase con error de concordancia en pasiva.
questions.question: Which sentence uses the passive INCORRECTLY?
options: The room is cleaned every day.
The house was painted last summer.
The homework are done by students.
The story was written by a journalist.
questions.explanation: 'Homework' es incontable y SIEMPRE singular → 'is done', nunca 'are done'. Error típico del hispanohablante: tratar 'homework' como plural (calcado de 'los deberes'). Otros incontables tramposos: news, information, advice, furniture, luggage.
examples: The homework is done every night before dinner. → incontable singular
The students' homework is checked daily by the teacher. → concordancia correcta

questions.statement: 'The novel wrote by Orwell' is a grammatically correct passive sentence.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Falta el AUXILIAR 'was' y el verbo debe ir en PARTICIPIO. Lo correcto: 'The novel was written by Orwell.' Error típico del hispanohablante: confundir past simple ('wrote') con participio ('written'). Verbos irregulares: write-wrote-written.
examples: The novel was written by Orwell in 1949. → pasiva correcta con participio
The song was composed by Mozart when he was very young. → misma estructura

questions.prompt: Describes una receta típica en una carta de restaurante.
questions.question: Choose the natural sentence:
options: This dish cook with olive oil.
This dish is cooked with olive oil.
This dish was cook with olive oil.
questions.explanation: 'Is cooked with' → pasiva presente simple para procesos habituales o recetas. El plato NO cocina, ES cocinado. Errores: (A) sin auxiliar; (C) 'cook' sin participio; (D) construcción imposible ('the dish cooks by chef').
examples: This bread is baked in a traditional wood-fired oven. → proceso descrito
This soup is served with fresh sourdough bread. → paso habitual en receta

questions.target: My phone was stolen at the concert last week, but luckily the police actually found it the next day.
questions.explanation: Situación: cuentas una anécdota de mala/buena suerte. Combina pasiva pasado ('was stolen') con activa pasado ('found'). Discourse markers 'luckily' y 'actually' añaden emoción real. Fórmula típica de storytelling: mala noticia + giro positivo.
examples: My laptop was damaged in the flight but the shop fixed it super quickly. → problema + solución
The window was broken by the storm but our neighbour helped us repair it. → daño + ayuda
